sections.title: What Is HuggingFace?
sections.body: > **HuggingFace is the GitHub of AI. It hosts 500,000+ models, 100,000+ datasets, and provides the libraries (transformers, datasets, PEFT, TRL, accelerate) that the entire AI industry uses to train, fine-tune, and deploy models.**

sections.title: HuggingFace Ecosystem Map
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              HUGGINGFACE COMPLETE ECOSYSTEM                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  THE HUB (huggingface.co):
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Models:    500,000+  (LLaMA, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen, Phi...)
  Datasets:  100,000+  (training data for any task)
  Spaces:    50,000+   (live demos, apps built on models)

  MODEL CARDS:
  Every model has a model card explaining:
  → What it does, how it was trained
  → License (MIT, Apache 2.0, Llama license, etc.)
  → How to use it with code examples
  → Performance benchmarks

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  THE LIBRARIES:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  transformers          → Load/run/fine-tune any model
  datasets              → Load/process training data
  tokenizers            → Fast tokenization (Rust-based)
  accelerate            → Multi-GPU, distributed training
  peft                  → LoRA, QLoRA, adapters
  trl                   → SFT, DPO, RLHF training
  diffusers             → Image generation models
  evaluate              → Metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, etc.)
  huggingface_hub       → Download/upload models/datasets
  optimum               → Hardware-optimized inference
  safetensors           → Safe, fast model file format

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  MODEL FILE FORMAT (safetensors):
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Old format (.bin / .pt):
  → PyTorch pickle files
  → Security risk (can execute arbitrary code when loaded!)
  → Slow to load (Python pickle)

  New format (.safetensors):
  → Safe (no code execution, just data)
  → Fast loading (memory-mapped, no deserialization)
  → Standard for all new HuggingFace models

  A model on HuggingFace typically looks like:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct/                   │
  │  ├── config.json            ← model architecture        │
  │  ├── tokenizer.json         ← tokenizer vocabulary      │
  │  ├── tokenizer_config.json  ← tokenizer settings        │
  │  ├── special_tokens_map.json← special tokens            │
  │  ├── generation_config.json ← generation defaults       │
  │  ├── model.safetensors.index.json  ← file index         │
  │  ├── model-00001-of-00004.safetensors  ← weights part 1 │
  │  ├── model-00002-of-00004.safetensors  ← weights part 2 │
  │  ├── model-00003-of-00004.safetensors  ← weights part 3 │
  │  └── model-00004-of-00004.safetensors  ← weights part 4 │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  Total: ~16 GB for LLaMA-3 8B in FP16

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  MODEL NAMING CONVENTION (how to read model names):
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  "meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct"
   ─────────── ──────────── ── ── ────────
   org/user    model family  v  params  variant

  Common variants:
  Base       → Raw pretrained, no instruction tuning
  Instruct   → Fine-tuned to follow instructions
  Chat       → Fine-tuned for conversation
  GPTQ       → Quantized with GPTQ
  AWQ        → Quantized with AWQ
  GGUF       → Converted to GGUF format

  Examples:
  "mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1"          → Base model
  "mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2" → Instruction tuned
  "TheBloke/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2-GPTQ" → GPTQ quantized
  "bartowski/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2-GGUF" → GGUF format
```

sections.title: HuggingFace Transformers — How It Works Internally
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         TRANSFORMERS LIBRARY — INTERNAL ARCHITECTURE            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  THE AUTO CLASSES (magic behind from_pretrained):
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("model_name")
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  1. Check local cache (~/.cache/huggingface/hub/)        │
  │  2. If not cached: download from HF Hub                 │
  │  3. Read tokenizer_config.json                          │
  │  4. Detect tokenizer type (BPE, WordPiece, SentencePiece)│
  │  5. Load vocabulary + merge rules                       │
  │  6. Return correct tokenizer class                      │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("model_name")
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  1. Read config.json → detect model architecture        │
  │  2. Instantiate correct model class                     │
  │     (LlamaForCausalLM, MistralForCausalLM, etc.)        │
  │  3. Download weights (safetensors files)                │
  │  4. Load weights into model                             │
  │  5. Return model ready for inference                    │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  THE PIPELINE (highest level API):
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  pipeline("text-generation", model="gpt2")
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Wraps: tokenizer + model + post-processing             │
  │  One function call = tokenize + generate + decode       │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  TOKENIZATION — HOW IT WORKS:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Text:  "Hello, how are you?"

  Step 1: BPE Tokenization
  "Hello"   → ["He", "llo"]      or  ["Hello"]  (depends on vocab)
  ","       → [","]
  " how"    → [" how"]
  " are"    → [" are"]
  " you"    → [" you"]
  "?"       → ["?"]

  Step 2: Convert to token IDs
  ["Hello", ",", " how", " are", " you", "?"]
  → [15496,   11,   703,   389,   345,   30]

  Step 3: Add special tokens
  <|begin_of_text|> 15496 11 703 389 345 30 <|end_of_text|>

  Step 4: Create attention mask
  [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]  ← 1 = real token, 0 = padding

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  GENERATION — HOW IT WORKS:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Input tokens: [1, 15496, 11, 703, 389, 345, 30]
       │
       ▼
  Transformer layers (attention + FFN × 32 layers)
       │
       ▼
  Output: probability distribution over ALL 128,000 tokens
  e.g.: {"Paris": 0.45, "London": 0.12, "France": 0.08, ...}
       │
       ▼
  SAMPLING STRATEGY (how to pick next token):
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Greedy:      always pick highest probability           │
  │  Temperature: divide logits by T before softmax         │
  │               T<1 = sharper (more confident)            │
  │               T>1 = flatter (more random)               │
  │  Top-K:       sample only from top K tokens             │
  │  Top-P:       sample from tokens summing to prob P      │
  │  Beam search: explore multiple sequences simultaneously │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
       │
       ▼
  Next token selected → append → repeat until stop condition
```
